title: Layout and spacing
instruction: Build each page on the column grid and spacing scale, readable at every width.
intro: Every page sits on a column grid and spaces its parts in steps of 8 px. The grid changes with the screen, from 12 columns on a desktop to four on a phone, and each paragraph spans the columns that keep its lines at the measure chapter 06 sets.
A page also has to read at 320 px wide, and with its text at twice the size, with nothing cut off and no scrolling sideways.

rules.title: Space comes in steps of the 8 px scale.
rule: Use the eleven steps of the spacing scale, from 4 px to 104 px, for every gap, padding and margin. Spaces around text are set in rem, so they grow with the reader’s text, and the grid’s gutters and page margins are set in px.

text: One rhythm lets the parts of different pages line up, and a reader senses the order before reading it. Steps of 8, with a 4 px half step for tight places, land on whole pixels on common screens. Our fifth edition kept the same 8 px rhythm; Edition 06 gives each step a token.

correct.caption: The scale at true size, and a card spaced on it: 24 px of padding, 8 px from label to heading and 16 px from heading to text.

failure.caption: Fails the scale. The same card with gaps of 22, 13 and 37 px. Each is near a step and none is one, so the card sits out of line with the page around it.

builders: Name a step by its multiple of 8 times 100: --oa-space-300 is 24 px and --oa-space-050 is 4 px. A value between steps means the layout is off, so move to the nearest step.

rules.title: Each page sits on the column grid for its width.
rule: Lay each page on the grid for its width: 12 columns at 1440 and 1024 px, eight at 768 px and four on phones, with the gutters and margins in the specifications. Every section of a page shares the same column lines.

text: When every section uses the same column lines, the eye finds the edge of each block in the same place, page after page. Our fifth edition switched among two- to six-column grids from section to section, so no column line ran the length of a chapter.
why.basis: Design judgment; Phase 0 design director audit

correct.caption: The five grids drawn at one quarter of true size, each column’s width worked out from the tokens.

failure.caption: Fails the grid. A page at 1440 px, drawn at one quarter size, whose three sections sit on three, five and two columns. Their edges never line up, so each section reads as a separate page.

specs.label: Wide, 1440 px
specs.value: 12 columns of 87.3 px, 24 px gutters, 64 px margins

specs.label: Desktop, 1024 px
specs.value: 12 columns of 56.7 px, 24 px gutters, 40 px margins

specs.label: Tablet, 768 px
specs.value: 8 columns of 67.0 px, 24 px gutters, 32 px margins

specs.label: Phone, 390 px
specs.value: 4 columns of 75.5 px, 16 px gutters, 20 px margins

specs.label: Small phone, 360 px
specs.value: 4 columns of 70.0 px, 16 px gutters, 16 px margins

builders: Build the grid with CSS grid: grid-template-columns: repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr)) with column-gap: var(--oa-layout-grid-wide-gutter), and the page margin as padding. Keep 360 px on the 4-column grid with 16 px margins; it also holds the 320 px reflow test.

rules.title: Body text spans the columns that hold its measure.
rule: Body text spans five of 12 columns at 1440 px, seven of 12 at 1024 px, six of eight at 768 px and all four on phones. Those spans hold the 60 to 75 characters a line that chapter 06 sets, and a block that spans more columns caps its text at the body measure.

text: The grid places a block, and its span keeps the lines readable. A paragraph run across all 12 columns at 1440 px measured 165 characters a line, more than twice the measure, while the five-column span measured 66.

correct.caption: The body span at each width, measured with the same paragraph in Inter at 17 px. Phones fall under 60 characters, which suits a small screen.

failure.caption: Fails the measure. Drawn at one quarter size, a paragraph spanning all 12 columns at 1440 px. It measured 165 characters a line.

specs.label: Wide, 1440 px
specs.value: 5 of 12 columns, 533 px, 66 characters a line

specs.label: Desktop, 1024 px
specs.value: 7 of 12 columns, 541 px, 66 characters a line

specs.label: Tablet, 768 px
specs.value: 6 of 8 columns, 522 px, 64 characters a line

specs.label: Phone, 390 px
specs.value: 4 of 4 columns, 350 px, 40 characters a line

specs.label: Small phone, 360 px
specs.value: 4 of 4 columns, 328 px, 38 characters a line

builders: Give body text both a span and a cap: grid-column: span 5 at the wide width and max-width: var(--oa-layout-measure-body-ideal). The cap is in rem, so it holds the measure when text grows.

rules.title: A heading sits closer to the text it introduces than to the block above.
rule: Leave at least twice as much space above a heading as below it. Sections part by 80 px, a label sits 32 px below the block above it and 8 px above what it names, and paragraphs part by 16 px.

text: Readers group what sits close together, a pattern designers call proximity. A heading with equal space above and below seems to belong to neither block, and the reader pauses to work out which one it names.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the Gestalt principle of proximity

correct.caption: A section at true size, its gaps drawn as bands: 48 px above the heading, 16 px below it and 16 px between paragraphs.

failure.caption: Fails proximity. The same section with 24 px above and below the heading, so it floats between the two blocks.

specs.label: Above a heading inside a section

builders: Put the space on the heading’s top margin, never on the bottom of the block above it, so the gap moves with the heading wherever it lands.

rules.title: Breakpoints are set in em, so larger text gets a narrower layout.
rule: Write media queries in em, which follows the reader’s text size: 90em for the wide layout, 64em for desktop and 48em for tablet, with the phone layout as the base. On a 1440 px screen, a reader at 150 percent text gets the tablet layout and a reader at 200 percent the phone layout, with fewer, wider columns for the larger words.

text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.4 Resize Text asks that text reach 200 percent with nothing lost. A breakpoint in px ignores the reader’s text size, so doubled text crowds a layout drawn for smaller words: five columns at 1440 px hold about 28 characters of 34 px text a line. In em, the layout steps down as the text grows, and the measure cap in rem keeps the line length.

correct.caption: The layout a reader gets by window width and text size, worked out from the em breakpoints.

failure.caption: Fails 1.4.4 in practice. With breakpoints in px, a reader at 200 percent text keeps the wide layout, and body text at 34 px in a five-column span runs about 28 characters a line.

builders: Media queries cannot read custom properties, so write the em value itself: @media (min-width: 64em). The token’s mediaQuery field in tokens.json holds each one.

rules.title: Every page reads at 320 px wide, with nothing lost.
rule: At 320 CSS px, the width of a small phone or a desktop window zoomed to 400 percent, a page shows all its content without scrolling sideways. Tables stack into one card per row. Only content that needs two dimensions, such as a wide data table or a specimen at true size, scrolls inside its own labeled frame.

text: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.10 Reflow asks for content at 320 CSS px with no loss of information and no scrolling in two directions. When the Phase 0 audit set our fifth edition at 320 px, the page ran 524 px wide and its contrast table lost its last column.

correct.caption: A 320 px frame at true size holding contrast pairs as stacked cards. Every pair, ratio and use stays in view.

failure.caption: Fails 1.4.10. The same pairs kept as a table in a 320 px frame. The last column falls past the edge, and a reader on a small phone never sees what each pair may carry.

specs.label: Reflow width
specs.value: 320 CSS px, on the small phone grid

specs.label: Text at 200 percent
specs.value: No clipped boxes and no sideways scroll at 1440 px

builders: Check every page at 320, 360 and 390 px with the shared rendered check. A frame that must scroll gets role="region", a name and tabindex="0", so a keyboard user can scroll it too.

sources: W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, W3C Recommendation, success criteria 1.4.4 and 1.4.10, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/.
